title: Timeouts above ~71 minutes fire too early. Tap the bug.
explain: ms * 1000 is done in 32 bits, because both values are uint32_t. It wraps above 4294967 ms (about 71 minutes). Only then the result is widened to uint64_t. Cast one operand first, so the multiplication is 64-bit.

title: The counter still gets corrupted, although bump() takes the lock. Tap the bug.
explain: let _ = does not keep the value. The guard is dropped at once, so interrupts are enabled again before COUNT changes. The lock protects nothing. Bind it to a name, like _guard. The guard then lives to the end of the block.

title: After a Motor is created, m.stop() causes a HardFault. Tap the bug.
explain: A class with virtual functions has a hidden vtable pointer. memset on this also zeroes that pointer. The next virtual call jumps through a null pointer. It is also undefined behavior for a non-trivial type. Use member initializers instead.

pr.title: Raise UART IRQ priority to stop lost bytes
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: We lose bytes at 921600 baud. Priority 0 is the highest, so the UART ISR can never wait for other interrupts.

explain: FreeRTOS on Cortex-M can only be called from ISRs with a priority number at or above configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY (5 here). Priority 0 is above that limit. FreeRTOS cannot mask it, so queue data can be corrupted. Keep the number at 5 or more. Use DMA or the FIFO for speed.

pr.title: Fix garbage at the end of UART DMA frames
pr.author: senior-dev
pr.body: STM32H7, D-cache on. DMA read old bytes from RAM. The buffer is now 32-byte aligned and the cache is cleaned before the DMA starts.

explain: Good. The CPU writes tx_buf into the D-cache, but DMA reads RAM. Clean writes the cache lines to RAM before DMA starts. The buffer is aligned to 32 bytes, and its size is a multiple of 32 (the Cortex-M7 cache line). So the clean does not touch neighbour variables.

pr.title: Add hysteresis to the heater relay
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: The relay clicked too often. Now it turns on below 38 C and off when the temperature is 40 C.

explain: temp_c is a float from an ADC formula. It almost never equals 40.0f exactly. The temperature goes from 39.9 to 40.1 and the heater stays on. Hysteresis is a good idea, but compare with >=. Between 38 and 40 nothing changes, so the relay keeps its state.

title: What does this print?
explain: sizeof gives size_t, which is unsigned. left is converted to size_t, so 10 - 12 wraps to a huge number. A huge number is > 0, so it prints room. The buffer is really too small. Compare before you subtract: left > 12.

title: What does this print?
explain: There is no comma after "green". The compiler joins neighbour string literals, so the second item is "greenblue". The array has 2 items and the code compiles without a warning. Menu tables and error-text tables often have this bug. Put one item per line and check the count.

title: A crystal needs a load capacitance of 12 pF. PCB stray capacitance is about 3 pF. Two equal capacitors go from the crystal pins to GND. Which value?
explain: The two capacitors are in series: C/2. Stray capacitance adds in parallel: CL = C/2 + Cstray. So C = 2 x (12 - 3) = 18 pF. 24 pF forgets the stray part. 9 pF forgets that two capacitors in series give half. A wrong load slows the start-up or shifts the frequency.

title: Noisy ADC readings: 5 things to check
bullets: Source impedance: a high-impedance sensor cannot charge the sampling capacitor. Add a buffer or a longer sample time.
Put an RC filter or 100 nF at the ADC pin, close to the MCU.
The ADC reads a ratio to VREF. If VREF is a noisy supply, the readings move. Use a clean reference.
Layout: keep analog traces away from switching nets (DC-DC, PWM). Return current should not flow under the ADC input.
Average samples (oversampling) only after the hardware is good. Software cannot fix a bad input.
